question: Does an authoritative, Denver-specific seasonal fact exist that this page could use to answer a genuinely useful practical question it currently doesn't cover?
source: City and County of Denver — Department of Transportation and Infrastructure, LeafDrop program (denvergov.org); corroborated by Denver Gazette (2026-10-11) and Denverite coverage of the same program
evidence: Denver runs an official free LeafDrop leaf/pumpkin composting drop-off program every fall (2026 run: October 5 - November 25), at three named city locations (Cherry Creek Transfer Station, Denver Parks and Recreation at 3685 Havana St, Central Platte Campus).

The program requires leaves bagged in PAPER bags only (no plastic), with branches/other materials removed first — a specific, checkable logistical detail a homeowner would need to know before relying on it instead of a hauler.

Mile High's existing seasonal-cleanout page mentions "Fall brings yard waste — branches, leaves, and general cleanup" but does not mention this municipal program at all, despite it being directly relevant to exactly the fall yard-waste scenario the page already discusses.
limitations: Phase 4 sanity-check (reviewed 2026-10-12), addressing four specific risks before this is treated as actionable: (1) TOPIC FIT — confirmed: the page's existing Fall section already discusses exactly this yard-waste/leaf scenario, so LeafDrop is directly on-topic, not a tangential add. (2) CURRENCY — accessed 2026-10-12, inside the confirmed 2026 window (Oct 5 - Nov 25); this evidence is ALREADY STALE outside that window and must be re-verified (dates, locations, bag requirements) against denvergov.org before any copy referencing it is published, not just reused from this file. (3) EVERGREEN-CONTENT RISK — LeafDrop's dates/locations are set annually by the city and are NOT safe to hardcode as static page copy with no maintenance plan; if this is acted on, the published wording should describe the PROGRAM generically ("the city runs a seasonal free leaf drop-off program each fall") and link to Denver's own LeafDrop page for the current year's specific dates/locations, rather than embedding "October 5 - November 25" as evergreen text that will be wrong next year. (4) VISITOR BENEFIT — still only PLAUSIBLE, not proven: this does not establish how many real visitors are unaware of LeafDrop already or that adding it would measurably help anyone, since no analytics/Search Console data is available to this agent. Also, as before: does NOT establish search volume or ranking impact — SERP/news presence is not the same as demonstrated visitor demand.
recommendation: A genuine, specific, locally-grounded FAQ-worthy question exists and is currently unanswered on this page: e.g. "Can I use Denver's free LeafDrop program instead of hauling?" (branches/mixed debris and anything beyond paper-bagged leaves still need a hauler; LeafDrop is seasonal and location-limited). This is a real content opportunity — NOT evidence that the page needs exactly 3 more FAQs to match its siblings' average; the 3-vs-6 question count was only the trigger for this research, not the target. Still requires a human to write accurate copy, phrased to avoid hardcoding this year's specific dates/locations (see limitations' evergreen-content note) and to verify currency against denvergov.org at publish time. Remains PROPOSE_CHANGE, not an auto-write.
